messages:
sam: heads-up — multiple customers (notably @AcmeAnalytics and @GreenRoad) reporting sudden 429s and higher latency for text-generation endpoints since ~09:05 UTC. We also got billing alerts about unexpected retry inflation.
tess: saw the alert too. throwing it to infra — might be limiter-related.
deploy-bot: deploy completed: id=deploy-2025-11-12-2244 image=services/limiter:v2.3.1 at 09:01 UTC
infra-ops: i'm on logs. quick glance shows limiter rejects starting ~09:04. sampling a trace now.
sam: can we get the limiter config that landed? org=acme-analytics
infra-ops: pasted from runtime on pod svc-gen-7:
```
rate_limiter:
  mode: bursty_token_bucket
  refill: 1
  refill_unit: minute
  max_burst: 100
  max_tokens: 1000
```
dee: wait — `refill: 1` with `refill_unit: minute` -> that's 1 token/minute not 1/sec. UI shows refill=1 (per-second). Looks like the deploy introduced a unit-interpretation change.
product-support: omg that would explain token starvation for bursty jobs. clients were doing quick retries which consumed tokens fast.
infra-ops: corroborating traces: client X made 40 quick requests in 10s, token refills were effectively 0 during that window -> queueing -> 429s. sample log:
```
[09:04:12] limiter: grant org=acme-analytics tokens_left=0
[09:04:12] limiter: reject org=acme-analytics route=/v1/generate reason=exhausted
[09:04:13] proxy: reply 429 to client=34.55.66.77 req_id=rd-zzb1
```

sam: mitigation? can we override for the affected orgs?
infra-ops: issuing emergency override now: set refill=1 refill_unit=second for orgs acme-analytics, greenroad, beta-shop. applied at 09:10 UTC. also rolling back limiter image to v2.3.0 on control plane.
deploy-bot: rollback started for service limiter-controller -> complete at 09:16 UTC
dee: after override and rollback, 429s dropped to baseline around 09:18.
billing-bot: note: there was an invoice alert at 09:07/09:09 due to retry traffic, blocked auto-sla guard invoked.
tess: customer comms?
sam: support reached out to AcmeAnalytics ops at 09:12, explained brief outage and applied credits offer. they asked for root cause.
product-support: RCA draft: deploy introduced a change where the UI and new runtime agreed on `refill` semantics but an intermediate config conversion script mistakenly translated `per_second` to `minute`. result: refill rate 60x lower than intended for all orgs that had per-second configs. the bug was in config-converter v1.4.
infra-ops: action items I will take:
- revert config-converter to v1.3 and add unit tests for time-unit edge cases
- add validator that rejects `refill_unit` values not in {second, minute, millisecond} and warns on conversions
- emit metric limiter.refill_effective_rate per-org and alert if it deviates > 10x from console config

sam: runbook updates please — we need an emergency knob and a canary for config-converter.
product-support: agree. also propose a gating rule: any config change that reduces effective refill below observed recent peak rps should be rejected.
dee: filed tickets: INFRA-9054 (config-converter revert + tests), RUNBOOK-411 (emergency override + canary), ALERTS-789 (refill_effective_rate alert).

sam: reproduction steps for QA and customers wanting to validate:
1) create org test-burst and set limiter refill=1 unit=second, burst=200
2) deploy config and send a 30-rps burst for 15s with client retries
3) observe tokens consumed and confirm no 429s
4) run conversion tool with per-second -> per-minute to validate detection

tess: follow-ups: confirm which customers got credits and tally estimated cost impact. I'll own the customer PM loop.
product-support: suggested mitigation to avoid future incidents: always deploy config-converter behind a 10% traffic canary that mirrors config outputs into a read-only namespace, then compare runtime vs console for mismatches.
infra-ops: agreed. adding automatic rollback if 429 rate > 3x baseline in first 10m after config change.
sam: timeline: deploy 09:01, 429s start 09:04, override/rollback 09:10-09:16, incidents quiet 09:18.
product-support: root cause = config-converter unit-interpretation bug + lack of canary + insufficient telemetry on per-org effective refill rate.
billing-bot: customers offered pro-rated credits: AcmeAnalytics and GreenRoad accepted 2 weeks.
sam: thanks all. assigning owners: infra-ops -> INFRA-9054, dee -> RUNBOOK-411, product-support -> customer comms and postmortem. closing when tickets complete and runbook updated. :thumbsup:
